title: Circuit symbols: reading a schematic

spans.text: Wires appear as lines and joined connections as dots. Recognizing resistor, capacitor, diode, and ground symbols helps explain how a circuit works. Do not assume crossing lines are connected unless the schematic shows a junction. Resistors are non-polar; electrolytic capacitors and diodes have an orientation.
Labels such as R1 and C1 identify parts; they are not the parts' values. The bar in a diode symbol marks its cathode, and outward arrows on an LED symbol represent emitted light.

visual_description: Add a wiring schematic and pin map showing board pins, VCC/GND, and signal direction; include a memory or task-state diagram where relevant.
